author: opus-5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Took over from gpt-5.6-sol. The earlier reuse only covered completed reads: it held the session lock for the whole response body, and cancelling reconnected. Replaced it with one session task that owns the provider socket. Each tap sends an opaque selection id. When a new selection arrives, the task sends {"type":"interrupt"} (the contract was agreed with the bridge owner), discards every frame up to that turn's turn_complete, and prompts the new read on the SAME socket. Parts of one combined row queue in order instead. Other changes: the lock wait is bounded (25 s); warm_up checks liveness and restarts a 5-minute idle clock; keepalive pings detect a dead path; a missing interrupt ack is bounded at 3 s; queued errors and write-then-read failures retry once on a fresh session; the /speak fallback shares the session; telemetry reports session/turn/session_reused/retried explicitly, and the four server phases now sum to request_to_first_audio. Regression switching_mid_turn_interrupts_and_begins_the_next_read_on_the_same_session consumes one A chunk, switches, and shows B on the single accepted socket as turn 2 with distinct audio and no late A PCM. Still open: exact-head deployment with the bridge interrupt support, and a live proof of both completed and interrupted A→B with tap-to-audible records.

author: opus-5.5
body:
[opus 5.5] Landed on main in bce56fa ("vibe-talk: play a streamed read-aloud through Web Audio as it arrives"). The page's own delivery path was the dominant remaining stage: Chromium's <audio src> buffers a streamed WAV by bytes, about 225 KB of samples before loadedmetadata, which is about 4.7 s of 24 kHz mono speech arriving at speaking pace, so tap-to-audible measured 5.2-5.7 s while the server's first audio was under 1 s. Other containers (MP3, Ogg, FLAC, WebM, AAC) still waited 3.8-4 s. The page now fetches the prepared URL itself and schedules the PCM on a Web Audio context as it arrives, with a 0.1 s lead that doubles on underrun up to 0.8 s. A switch, a stop or leaving Read aborts the fetch, so closing the response still interrupts the server-side turn; a response cut off part-way is an error and archives nothing; browsers without streamed fetch bodies or Web Audio fall back to <audio>. make -C vibe-talk read-aloud-browser (now also run by root make validate) measures about 160 ms tap-to-audible and 149 ms after a switch against an <audio> negative control at about 4.8 s, and asserts from the real AudioBufferSourceNodes that the switched-away read's queued audio is stopped at the switch; it fails on the unfixed page and on a mutation that leaves that audio playing.

Live on the deployed build, 2026-09-25 17:02-17:12Z, headless Chromium with a phone user agent plus an HTTP-only driver (no physical phone, so a real phone remains unverified). The page layer passes: every tap reached audible 130-170 ms after the server's first audio (first read 723 ms; B after a completed A 559 ms page / 43 ms HTTP), a switch left 0 of A's queued sources sounding, Stop left 0 of B's, and the audio context was suspended after Stop. Completed and interrupted A->B each stayed on one session with consecutive turns and reuse, and the interrupted turn ended interrupted+superseded.

Keep open for two defects in the voice services behind the bridge, both reproduced by the HTTP driver without any browser, so the page cannot cause them:
D1. A turn requested right after an interrupt waits about 8.1-8.4 s for first audio (2 of 2), against 41-408 ms after a completed turn. The cancelled response's paced tail delays the next one.
D2. After an interrupt, a session left idle (25 s and 78 s observed) never starts the next turn; after 10 s it reports "turn N never started after an interrupt; reconnect" and the read retries on a new session, about 10.4 s to first audio (2 of 2).
Acceptance for this issue: rerun interrupted A->B and idle-after-interrupt live once the voice-side fix is deployed, with B's first audio in line with the completed case and no reconnect.

Non-blocking notes still open from review, for a later commit: an odd trailing byte at the end of the body is dropped silently; the AudioContext 'interrupted' state some mobile browsers use is not resumed (only 'suspended' is); there may be slight clicks at the seams between separately resampled 24 kHz buffers; and, pre-existing on the server, speak_stream ends the body cleanly if the turn channel closes without a Failed event, so a cut-off turn can look complete to <audio> and the new player alike.
